verdict.rationale: Several independent hands-on reports confirm that Sentry's core product can be self-hosted, via git clone plus ./install.sh or a Helm chart, and has run in production for years. Other reports add real caveats: self-hosted releases lag the SaaS version, the full feature set needs at least 16GB of RAM, and setups often need Kafka/Redis tuning or are called 'increasingly prohibitively complex'. missing for 10: first-party self-hosting documentation in the evidence pack, feature parity with SaaS, lightweight deployment that suits smaller setups.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: A user has run self-hosted Sentry at work for a couple of years and says it has worked fantastically and is rock-solid once running.
installation is git clone, editing one or two config files, and running ./install.sh
A user deployed self-hosted Sentry with a Helm chart and says it 'just works'.
Sentry was straightforward to deploy years ago but is now 'self host-able but increasingly prohibitively complex'.
